thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Rally Fueled by Renewed U.S./China Trade Talks

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Wall Street Rally Fueled by Renewed U.S./China Trade Talks
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Rally Fueled by Renewed U.S./China Trade Talks August 16, 2018, 04:37:21 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Powered by strong quarterly results from Walmart ( WMT ) and Cisco ( CSCO ) and positive developments on the U.S./China trade front, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied by more than 400 points on Thursday, its biggest one-day gain since April. Higher Treasury yields bolstered the financial sector, while industrials were shored up by the weaker dollar and chances for a trade deal with China.
Wall Street set aside Turkey's currency and financial crisis and shifted focus to the upcoming trade talks with China at the end of the month. Shares in trade-sensitive companies like Boeing ( BA ), Caterpillar ( CAT ) and Apple ( AAPL ) outperformed with Apple setting another all-time high.
This morning's economic data failed to dent the bull run in stocks even as the Philadelphia Fed business outlook index fell to its lowest level since Nov 2016, and July housing starts were down year-over-year for the second month in a row. On the plus side, jobless claims fell another 2,000 to 212,000 for the week ending Aug 11.
In earnings news, Walmart lunged to its highest level since February after handily beating Wall Street's expectations and hiking its full year EPS guidance above estimates. Blue chip stock Cisco reported better-than-expected gains in profit and sales, lifting its stock price to within striking distance of its all-time high. Shares of JC Penney (JCP), however, tumbled to their lowest level on record as the company's Q2 loss widened more than expected and revenue fell 8% from a year ago. Any negative fallout on the consumer sector was mitigated by Walmart's outsized gain of 10%.
Tesla (TSLA) shares were down for a third straight day, wiping out all of its "go-private" gain from last week as worries mount that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission will investigate whether CEO Elon Musk was plotting against shorts in his now famous tweet.
Thursday's risk-on trade was reflected in the poor price action of safe-havens. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note increased 4 basis points; gold fell to its lowest level in 19 months; and the yen and Swiss franc were both lower against the US dollar.
Friday's economic data includes the preliminary Univ of Michigan consumer sentiment index for August (est 97.9), and July leading economic indicators (est +0.4%) both at 10am ET. At 1:00pm ET, the Baker Hughes rig count will be released.
